item.title: Report: Court notification on reopening Mount Meron disaster investigation delayed by one month
item.description:
Police and prosecutors had planned to inform the Supreme Court on Thursday that the criminal investigation into the Mount Meron disaster would be reopened. However, the police legal adviser requested a one-month delay in submitting the notification, according to a report in Haaretz.
According to the report, the legal adviser, who is close to Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana, justified the request by citing the need to clarify certain matters with Police Commissioner Dani Levy.

item.title: Update: Three children, one adult killed in Oregon elementary school shooting
item.description: At least three children and one adult killed in a shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon. Suspect shot and killed.

item.title: IDF clarifies: Ramming near Ateret was not terror attack, driver transferred to security forces
item.description:
The IDF Spokesperson's Unit clarified, "Following the incident in the area of Ateret, an initial inquiry determined that the incident was not terror-related."
The driver was transferred to security forces, and officers from the Judea and Samaria District Police opened an investigation to establish the circumstances of the accident.

item.title: Several injured, including children, in shooting at Oregon elementary school
item.description: Several people, including children, injured in a shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon. Police say the gunman is dead and at least two were hospitalized.

item.title: Interceptor launched toward false target in southern Lebanon, no sirens sounded
item.description:
A short while ago, an interceptor was launched toward a false target identified in the area in which IDF soldiers are operating in southern Lebanon, the IDF Spokesperson's Unit said.
No sirens were sounded in accordance with protocol.

item.title: Incoming UTJ MK compares yeshiva students' situation to Holocaust era
item.description: Elyakim Shtark compares yeshiva students' fears of arrest at airports to restrictions on crossing borders during the Holocaust.

item.title: Show of strength in Jerusalem: 5,000 attend Religious Zionist Party rally
item.description: More than 5,000 activists and leading religious Zionist rabbis attend rally in Jerusalem. Smotrich warns voters against taking risks in the upcoming elections.

item.title: Ramming incident in Binyamin: Security officials believe it was not a terror attack
item.description: Following an initial investigation, Israeli security officials believe that the ramming incident near the community of Ateret in the Binyamin region, in which one person was reportedly lightly injured, was not a terrorist attack.

item.title: Suspected ramming attack in Binyamin, one injured, suspect at large

item.title: Initial report of ramming near Ateret in Binyamin
item.description: A person was reportedly lightly injured in a suspected ramming attack near Ateret in Binyamin. According to the report, the suspect fled the scene.

item.title: Draft evaders barred from civil service jobs under new enforcement rules
item.description: Draft-eligible individuals who fail to regularize their status must provide IDF clearance within five days of winning a civil service tender or risk losing the job.

item.title: District Court overturns decision to release Samaria security official
item.description:
The District Court accepted the police appeal and overturned the decision regarding the security official from Samaria, whose identifying details are under a gag order.
His detention was extended by an additional five days, and he is expected to be transferred to an Israel Prison Service facility on Sunday. The judge asked law enforcement authorities to consider an earlier transfer and even his release before the end of the detention period.

item.title: Drama at wedding: Groom’s father collapses, is resuscitated and regains consciousness
item.description: A man in his 60s collapsed at his son’s wedding. Guests performed CPR and delivered three defibrillator shocks before MDA paramedics restored his pulse and he regained consciousness.

item.title: Riot in Jerusalem's Abu Tor neighborhood, building and vehicle set on fire
item.description:
A violent riot broke out in the Abu Tor neighborhood of Jerusalem following a suspected murder and against the backdrop of an ongoing dispute between families.
According to police, a residential building and a vehicle were apparently set on fire during the riot. Police officers and Border Police forces are working to restore order, while firefighting crews were dispatched to the scene. No injuries have been reported at this stage.

item.title: Amb. Danon warns Hezbollah: 'Do not attempt to exploit Israel’s election period'
item.description: Israel’s Ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon, issues a direct warning to Iran and Hezbollah: 'Anyone who dares to attack us will face a devastating response.'

item.title: Report: Israel raised alert level over a possible security threats to elections
item.description:
Israel has raised its level of alert in recent days amid concerns over a possible security escalation, less than two weeks before the elections, Kan News reported.
At this stage, there is no concrete information indicating that Iran or Hezbollah intends to attack, but the IDF is monitoring missile and drone tests being conducted by Iran.
A security official said: “We are acting to ensure that we are not caught by surprise."

item.title: Trump cancels planned livestream of Fort Hood terrorist's execution
item.description: President Donald Trump announces that Nidal Hasan's execution will proceed by firing squad, but will not be broadcast to the public. Victims' immediate families will be permitted to attend.

item.title: Horror in a suitcase: 92 venomous reptiles discovered at German airport
item.description: Customs officers were stunned to find 37 live venomous snakes and 55 lizards hidden in a Mexican passenger’s suitcase, concealed in shampoo bottles, socks and clothing.

item.title: More than 25 years later: Second 9/11 victim identified through new DNA technology
item.description: New York City officials have identified another victim of the September 11 terrorist attacks using advanced genetic genealogy, bringing the total number of identified victims to 1,655.

item.description: IDF and ISA eliminated two terrorists who facilitated the smuggling of weapons and military equipment into Gaza.

item.description: B'Tsalmo calls on Assaf Rappaport, who is in advanced talks to acquire the McDonald's Israel franchise, to end the chain's longstanding absence from Judea and Samaria.
